messages:
sam_cs: Hey team — ACME (acct ACME-22) filed an escalation: their quantized endpoint (rdx-7b-4bit, calibrated last week) is both slower and lower-quality than their FP16 variant. They attached p95 graphs and example requests. Can we triage?

maria_runtime: Thanks — can you paste a representative request + config (seq lengths, avg batch size, prompt examples)?

sam_cs: pasted sample: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rdx-7b-4bit/generate 
-H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" 
-d '{"input":"Summarize the following:\n...","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.2}'
```
Most traffic is short-turn chat, seq <= 64, batch_size usually 1-2. p95 FP16 ~= 110-140ms, p95 4-bit ~= 450-700ms depending on time of day.

aj_oncall: Running repro harness now (loadgen against their same payloads). Repro is clean: FP16 p95 ~120ms, 4bit p95 ~560ms on canary node.

leo_perf: If you can share a profile dump I can look for kernel fallbacks / memcpy hotspots. Initial guess: kernel selection choosing a slow quant path or KV cache thrash.

sam_cs: uploaded runtime traces and the graph they sent (p95 spike aligned with calibration rollout).

runtime-bot: [deploy-bot] Calibration rollout 2026-03-02T03:12Z applied to model rdx-7b-4bit in prod/us-east-1.

maria_runtime: Looking at traces: kernel selection log shows this for a sample request:
```
selected_kernel: quant_attn_v2_dequant -> aten_matmul -> requant_store
kv_mode: enabled
kv_cache_layout: legacy_interleaved
```
Notably we see an extra dequant/requant stage between attention kernels. That generates device->host and host->device memcpy for some code paths because of incompatible tensor layouts.

leo_perf: Microbenchmarks: the new quant_attn_v2 gives good throughput for long sequences (>=512) but is ~3x slower than the fused FP16 kernel for seq <= 64, especially at batch_size=1. That matches ACME usage.

aj_oncall: Also seeing KV cache eviction churn in traces — calibration metadata changed byte packing for cached KV which caused our caching layer to reserialize entries, adding overhead per request.

maria_runtime: Root cause hypothesis: the calibration roll changed quant kernel selection + KV cache layout assumptions. For short sequences and single-request batches this forces a slow dequant->attn->requant path and causes extra memcpys and KV resyncs. Net result: higher latency and occasional small quality diffs from extra rounding.

leo_perf: Repro script: 
```
python perf/run_microbench.py --model rdx-7b --mode quantized --seq 32 --bs 1 --profile
# shows kernel timings: 
# fused_fp16_attn: 12ms
# quant_dequant_attn_seq32: 42ms
# memcpy_host: 28ms
```
So memcpys are a big chunk.

maria_runtime: Mitigations (short-term):
- Route ACME traffic to fp16 variant (cheap roll-back) OR
- Enable alternate kernel selection that prefers fused path for seq<=128 (config toggle) OR
- Turn on prefix/KV sticky caching to avoid reserialization.
All are doable; rollback is fastest.

aj_oncall: I recommend routing rule rollback for ACME immediately to restore latency while we fix kernel selection. Canary shows rollback brings p95 back to ~130ms.

sam_cs: I'll prepare customer comms. Proposed message: "We investigated — calibration caused quant runtime to pick a slow short-sequence path. We will route your traffic back to the FP16 variant for now and work on a targeted runtime fix. Expected impact: latency back to prior levels within 1 hour." Thoughts? :thumbsup:

leo_perf: +1. Also propose a perf-safe hotfix: when KV cache is enabled and seq<=128, prefer kernel fusion path or avoid intermediate re-layouts. I'll draft a patch.

maria_runtime: I've created INF-7832 documenting traces, benchmarks, and repro steps. Assigning to leo_perf for kernel change and to infra for routing rule.

runtime-bot: [infra-bot] Routing rule change scheduled: route ACME-22 -> rdx-7b-fp16 (canary1 -> prod) at 1955554500.

aj_oncall: Rollback executed at 1955554500. Post-rollback numbers on the same canary: p95 = 128ms (stable). Traces show fused_fp16_attn path restored and memcpy hotspot gone.

sam_cs: Customer confirmed improved latency and accepted rollback. Sending formal update now with apology and followups.

maria_runtime: Next actions:
- leo_perf to submit kernel-selection hotfix PR (prefer fused path for short seq when kv enabled) — target canary deploy tomorrow morning.
- infra to add a routing policy flag "prefer_fast_short_seq" with default false until tested.
- CS to coordinate a joint call with ACME next week to discuss potential cost delta from FP16 routing and timeline for fix.

leo_perf: PR opened (link: https://git.redwood/rdx/PR/5123) — changes: kernel selector now inspects kv_cache_layout + requested seq and avoids dequant path for seq<=128 where we have fused alternative. Benchmarks in PR show p95 parity with FP16 for short sequences.

runtime-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deploy scheduled for PR 5123 tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

sam_cs: Thanks all. I'll keep this thread updated with customer notes and impact. Marking INF-7832 as triaged. :white_check_mark:

aj_oncall: closing loop — issue mitigated for ACME via rollback; follow-on fixes in flight.

maria_runtime: follow-up: document calibration -> kv layout compatibility matrix so future rollouts include KV serialization compatibility checks.

sam_cs: Noted. I'll include that in the postmortem for the customer.
